title: Telemetry Onboarding, Provisioning, and Service Deprecation Runbook for Private Deploys
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Purpose
=======

This runbook describes the operator-facing and customer-facing process for onboarding telemetry, provisioning observability contracts, and safely deprecating telemetry APIs or events for Redwood private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. It is intended for operators, SREs, and customer engineering teams who own private deploy rollouts and day-2 telemetry lifecycle.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: telemetry ingestion, sampling, schema contracts, retention classes, alerting, metrics/trace/log collection endpoints, and the organized steps for removing or retiring telemetry signals.
- Audience: Private Deploy Operators, Customer Onboarding Engineers, Observability Engineers, Product Owners, and Support.

Summary of approach
--------------------
1) Standardize a minimal observability contract that every private deployment must provide to Redwood and the customer.
2) Onboard telemetry in three phases: smoke, steady-state, and regulated.
3) Provision sampling/retention that minimizes customer data exposure while preserving the ability to debug incidents.
4) Offer a clear deprecation path for telemetry events with safe rollback and customer communication templates.

Telemetry contract (must-haves)
--------------------------------
All private deployments must expose these items to meet the Redwood support and upgrade SLAs: 

- Ingestion endpoints: metrics (Prometheus or PushGateway endpoint), traces (OTLP/OTel over gRPC), and logs (structured JSON via Fluentd/Loki push).
- Heartbeat metric: redwood_runtime_heartbeat{tenant,region,env} gauge, emitted every 15s; expired if not seen for 60s.
- Request-level trace span: redwood.request (latency + status) with tags: tenant_id, model_name, route, shard_id, cold_start boolean.
- KV cache consistency event: redwood.kv_cache_miss{tenant,model} counter.
- Runtime resource metrics: gpu_utilization_percent, gpu_memory_free_mb, cpu_utilization_percent per node.

Operational SLOs and thresholds
-------------------------------
- Telemetry ingestion availability: 99.9% (per-tenant) within 30s of emission.
- Sampling fidelity: key user-facing trace spans captured for 95% of requests over steady-state.
- Alerting latency: critical telemetry alerts must reach oncall within 60s.

Table: telemetry event catalog (example)
--------------------------------------
Event Name | Required Fields | Expected Frequency | Retention Class
redwood_runtime_heartbeat | tenant_id, region, timestamp, pod_id | 4/min per pod | hot (30d)
redwood.request | tenant_id, request_id, model, latency_ms, status_code | per request | hot-warm (90d/365d)
redwood.kv_cache_miss | tenant_id, model, key_hash, timestamp | on miss | warm (180d)
redwood.model.swap | tenant_id, old_model, new_model, initiated_by | on model swap | audit (365d)

(When inserting into Confluence, this should be a proper table block; keep CSV-like if editing from CLI.)

Onboarding checklist (operator steps)
------------------------------------
1. Preflight: validate network & firewall rules
   - Ensure customer VPC allows outbound gRPC/443 to telemetry ingestion proxies when using hosted telemetry.
   - Validate local egress policies if telemetry is routed to the customer's observability stack instead.
2. Provision credentials and IAM
   - Create or verify service account with least privilege for telemetry delivery.
   - Document KMS/HSM usage for token storage.
3. Deploy agent and configuration
   - Install OTel collector or Fluentd daemonset using the packaged private runtime image. Example OTel YAML sample:

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
processors:
  batch:
exporters:
  otlp/remote: 
    endpoint: "ingest.redwood.example:4317"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/remote]
```

4. Validate signal presence
   - Smoke test: curl the heartbeat metric endpoint locally and confirm redwood_runtime_heartbeat appears.
   - Trace test: issue a synthetic request with request_id=test-telemetry-<YYYYMMDD> and verify a corresponding redwood.request span.
5. Configure sampling & retention
   - Start with a conservative sampling policy: 1/1 for canaries, 1/10 for steady-state traffic, and 1/100 for background bulk jobs.
   - Confirm retention classes in the customer's observability config (hot/warm/audit).
6. Set alerts and dashboards
   - Ensure these alerts exist: Telemetry Ingestion Failure (>=5% drop over 5m), Heartbeat Missing (>60s), High Trace Latency (>95th percentile > 2s).
   - Deploy tenant-specific dashboards in the operator console.
7. Signoff and handoff
   - Customer acceptance: run the acceptance test suite (see related page) and capture a signed checklist.

Deprecation and retirement of telemetry signals
----------------------------------------------
We require a 3-stage deprecation model for any telemetry event or field removal to preserve customer debuggability and compliance:

Stage 1 — Announcement (T0)
- Announce planned deprecation at least 90 days before removal. Provide rationale and migration guidance.
- Share a mapping table of old_event -> new_event or removal_reason.
- Internal: create a deprecation ticket, assign owner, and add to the release notes index.

Stage 2 — Warning window (T0 + 45d)
- Emit a runtime warning metric: redwood.telemetry.deprecation_notice{event=<name>,tenant}.
- Update SDK and agent to log a single telemetry warning to the operator console when the deprecated field is observed.
- Run compatibility checks in customer staging, offering an SDK compatibility shim if needed.

Stage 3 — Removal and rollback plan (T0 + 90d)
- Remove the event from production. Keep a preserved ingestion path that captures the deprecated event to a cold audit store for 365 days for forensic purposes.
- Rollback plan: re-enable the event via feature flag within 24 hours if customer critical issues arise. Operators must be prepared to toggle feature flag and redeploy agent config.

Customer communication templates (short)
--------------------------------------
- Initial notice email subject: [Action Required] Upcoming telemetry change for your Redwood private deployment
- Body highlights: what is changing, why, how to test, migration example, contact for support, and timelines.

Safe rollback cookbook (technical)
---------------------------------
1. Detect: product owner or customer reports regressions tracing to missing spans/metrics.
2. Triage: check preserved audit store for the deprecated events and verify absence in current ingestion pipeline.
3. Rollback path A (fast): toggle telemetry feature flag in the control plane and push new OTel config to agents. Commands (example):
   - rctl feature-set telemetry.keep_deprecated_event=true --tenant=<tenant_id>
   - kubectl rollout restart ds/otel-collector -n redwood-<tenant>
4. Rollback path B (longer): re-open temporary patch to the runtime that re-emits the field at source and validate end-to-end.
5. Post-incident: capture RCA, update runbook with cause, and schedule a follow-up compatibility shim if required.

Privacy, sampling and platform limits
------------------------------------
- Default max retention for hot telemetry is 30 days for private deployments unless contractually extended. Audit retention (model.swap, config changes) is 365 days minimum.
- Sampling must be privacy-aware; avoid sampling identifiable user content. Instrument pseudonymous ids and respect customer DLP rules.
- For airgapped customers with no outbound telemetry, provide the offline ingestion bundle and handshake instructions in the onboarding packet.

Example: sample alert rule (Prometheus)
-------------------------------------
ALERT TelemetryIngestionDown
IF increase(redwood_runtime_heartbeat[2m]) == 0
FOR 2m
LABELS {severity="critical"}
ANNOTATIONS {summary="Telemetry ingestion missing for a tenant or region"}

Operational run cadence and responsibilities
------------------------------------------
- Day 0 (Onboarding): Customer Engineering leads the install, Operator validates telemetry.
- Day 1-14 (Observation): SRE monitors ingestion, tunes sampling, and rebalances exporters.
- Ongoing: Operator runs weekly telemetry health check (scripted) and monthly data-retention audit.
- Ownership: Customer engineering (onboarding), Observability team (pipeline), SRE (alerts & escalations).

Checklist for retiring a telemetry endpoint (quick)
------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Publish deprecation notice (90d).
- [ ] Add runtime warning metric and SDK logs (45d).
- [ ] Validate migration in customer staging (30d window).
- [ ] Configure cold-audit capture on removal (365d).
- [ ] Prepare operator rollback flag and test rollback (before removal).

FAQ and troubleshooting tips
---------------------------
Q: A customer says they lost the ability to debug a latency regression after we removed a field. What do we do?
A: Re-enable deprecated event via feature flag, then inspect cold-audit store to map requests and run RCA. Follow the rollback cookbook above.

Q: How do we balance telemetry cost vs. coverage for very large customers?
A: Move non-critical signals to higher sampling or to warm retention classes; negotiate retention SLAs as part of the Dedicated/Private contract. Versioned quantization and prefix sampling can reduce volume for embeddings and large payloads.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
-------------------------------------
- Verify heartbeat: curl http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep redwood_runtime_heartbeat
- Restart collector: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/otel-collector -n redwood-tenant
- Export an event sample to local file (otel-cli): otel-cli exec -- curl "http://localhost:8000/health" --trace > sample_trace.json
